fixes.title: The cull rail advertises 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' from a curve it already knows is stale; pressing it always refuses
fixes.summary: Closed before this wave. session_review_controller.dart:1536-1581 exposes `cullRecommendationOffer`, which applies the whole staleness test (population length, duplicate paths, population-vs-accepted divergence, keepN >= population, gainPct <= 0) at RENDER time; cullToRecommended() at :1589-1599 now switches on that same getter instead of re-deriving it, so render and press can no longer disagree. sub_cull_rail.dart:289 gates the action on `_offer.isOfferable` and :503/:515 render an explanatory chip for the stale / already-optimal cases instead of a quantified button.
fixes.revert_check: Reverted sub_cull_rail.dart:289 `_offer.isOfferable ? ... : null` to `_offer.keepN > 0 ? ... : null` (the pre-fix condition). 4 of 4 tests failed, incl. 'a stale curve renders an out-of-date chip, not a quantified "Keep best N" action'. Restored: all pass.
fixes.caveats: Verified by reading the current source and revert-checking; not re-driven live (needs a session with real FITS subs).

fixes.summary: Closed before this wave. stack_and_share_service.dart:400-432 wraps the follower `_addStackFrame` await in a try/catch that counts the frame, records the reason, emits progress and CONTINUES; only a loss of provider authority still propagates. :459-466 fails the run only when nothing but the reference survived, naming the dominant reason, instead of persisting a one-frame 'stack'.

fixes.title: Registration reports a 10.34px residual for a pure 2.2px translation of the same 40-star field
fixes.summary: Closed before this wave, and closed at the cause rather than by moving a threshold. stacking.rs:834-919 adds `fit_transform_robust`: it fits, measures each pair's post-fit deviation, clips anything beyond 3x the MEDIAN deviation (floored at 1.5px), refits, up to 5 passes, never below a fittable set. add_frame (:490-497) now uses it, so the residual is the RMS over the pairs that agree rather than over every greedy nearest-neighbour pairing — which is what the 50px match radius poisoned. Only with that in place does the ceiling mean anything, so :97 tightens max_alignment_residual_px from 10.0 to 2.0, and :499-513 rejects a frame whose inlier count falls under min_matched_pairs with a message that names the disagreement.
fixes.revert_check: Reverted the add_frame call site to `compute_affine_transform` + `compute_alignment_residual` over all matches (inlier_count = matches.len()). add_frame_survives_a_matcher_cascade_from_missing_stars FAILED at stacking.rs:2639; the other 26 stacking tests still passed, so the end-to-end wiring is what the test holds. Restored: 27/27 pass, cargo fmt --check clean.
fixes.caveats: The verifier's alternative cause — that detect_stars may return bad centroids (it reads 0 stars on a frame an independent peak finder reads as 40) — is a separate detector-sensitivity question and is NOT addressed here. On-sky/real-FITS revalidation of the original two frames is still owed.

fixes.title: First Light's 'Could not load candidates' Retry does not re-query
fixes.summary: Closed before this wave, and at the real link (the Retry button already called ref.invalidate; the dead part was downstream). transient_detections_provider.dart:163-175 makes the local feed `yield await dao.recentDetections(...)` first and only then `yield* dao.watchRecentDetections(...).skip(1)`. Drift caches a query stream by its SQL and a cached stream that has thrown stays thrown for the process, so re-subscribing — all ref.invalidate can do — replayed the failure; a fresh one-shot read re-executes the query, and the .skip(1) stops the cached stream's stale replay from undoing it.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/first_light_candidates_resilience_test.dart — 'a fixed row is picked up by a re-subscription, not only by a restart'
fixes.revert_check: Removed the leading one-shot read and dropped the .skip(1). The test failed. Restored: passes.
fixes.caveats: The finding's second claim — that the list is fetched once per app launch — was not confirmed by the verifier either; the provider is a live Drift watch, and the external sqlite3 edit used in the repro is invisible to Drift's stream store by design. One narrow residual I looked at and deliberately left alone: the `.skip(1)` drops the watch stream's replay, and a write landing between the one-shot read and the subscription would be carried only by that replay, so it would wait for the next change notification. The window is microseconds inside one isolate, and closing it means subscribing before reading, which reintroduces the stale-replay problem the fix exists to solve. The remote (NetworkBackend) branch has no such issue: _remoteFirstLightStream builds a fresh controller and refetches per provider build, so Retry re-fetches there too.

fixes.title: Confirming a First Light candidate does not update the Observing Alerts tab beside it
fixes.summary: Wave 5 fixed the reported surface but left the same defect on three others, so this wave finished it. The cause is that `transientAlertStatesProvider` holds ONLY the queue/dismiss actions taken through the alert surfaces, and reading that map bare falls back to newAlert for any alert whose state lives on itself (First Light detections, via transientAlertFromDetection). transient_alert_provider.dart:924-929 already exposes `resolveTransientAlertState(alert, overrides)`; Observing Alerts (transients_screen.dart:180, :213-225) and the badge count were routed through it, but three consumers were not, so one confirmed detection still read 'Confirmed' on Observing Alerts and 'NEW' in the status-bar dropdown and the suggestions panel. Routed through the shared resolver: transient_alert_badge.dart:433 (dropdown NEW chip), transient_alerts_panel.dart:131 (tile state) and :206-207 (the actionable-first sort, which put confirmed alerts back at the top), and apps/desktop transient_handlers.dart:70-84/:278-284/:334-339 (the /api/transients active filter, dismissed/queued counts and the per-alert isQueued/isDismissed flags). Also wrapped the dropdown header title in a Flexible+ellipsis (transient_alert_badge.dart:346-357) — the fixed ~280px popup overflowed it under a wide text scale.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/alert_state_across_surfaces_test.dart (4 tests: the suggestions panel and the status-bar dropdown each must not re-badge a confirmed detection NEW, and must still badge an unconfirmed one) + apps/desktop/test/headless_api/transient_handlers_detection_state_test.dart (2 tests: a dismissed alert is not served as active and is counted dismissed; an undismissed one is served with isDismissed false). The pre-existing packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/transients_confirmed_state_test.dart covers the Observing Alerts surface wave 5 fixed.
fixes.revert_check: Reverted all three production sites at once — badge back to `states[alert.id]` with a null fallback, panel tile back to `alertStates[limited[i].id]`, handler back to `states[a.id] != dismissed` / `_countState(states, ...)` / `states[alert.id] == dismissed`. Failures: 'suggestions panel a confirmed detection is not re-badged NEW', 'status-bar alert dropdown a confirmed detection is not re-badged NEW', 'a detection dismissed in the app is not served as an active alert'. Restored: 12/12 app transients tests and 6/6 desktop transient-handler tests pass. Separately revert-checked wave 5's Observing Alerts fix by putting transients_screen.dart back to `states[alert.id]`: both transients_confirmed_state_test.dart assertions failed.
fixes.caveats: The /api/transients change is consistency hardening rather than a live-observable fix: that endpoint's alert list comes from TransientAlertService.getAllAlerts, which fetches only the external upstreams, so no First Light detection reaches it today (they have their own /api/firstlight/candidates endpoint). Whether the headless alert feed SHOULD merge First Light detections the way the in-app provider does is a separate question this wave did not open. The two mutation endpoints (queue/dismiss) still echo a count over the overrides map alone — resolving there would need a network fetch of the alert population on every mutation — and that is now stated at the helper.
